paragraphs: Rav Shisha son of Rav Idi, whose father was Avin the carpenter. Since some places have Rav Sheshet son of Rav Idi bar Avin, Yuhasin made a separate entry for each. It seems to me they are one; since most places have Rav Shisha, I wrote him here. Ta'anit 13a: Rav Idi bar Avin said, etc.; Abaye told him, etc.; Rav Shisha son of Rav Idi said, ‘This is what troubled my father.’ It thus proves Rav Shisha was Rav Idi bar Avin's son. Zevahim 6a and Eruvin 102a have Rav Sheshet; there, b, and Zevahim 14b, Rav Shisha. Heilprin’s Shabbat 138b reading is Rav Ashi son of Rav Idi, with Sheshet in what he calls the new Talmud editions and in the next statement. The checked Bavli has Sheshet both times. Heilprin reports Shishi in Asheri, the new editions and Rif. The checked Rosh and Rif read Shisha. Rosh Hashanah 7b: Rav Shisha bar Rav Idi. R' Yehoshua was his brother (see there); they are described as בני סמכי [ordination-status wording; precise sense unresolved], and their mother was a priest's daughter. Rav Shishi son of Rav Idi expounded in R' Yohanan's name: Shabbat 146b. Rav Mordekhai told Rav Ashi, ‘Thus Rav Shishi bar Rav Idi said’: Menahot 21b [the checked text has Shisha]. He spoke to Rav Pappa: Bava Metzia 109a. Heilprin gives Rav Sheshet bar Rav Idi at Bava Batra 8a [the checked text has Shisha]. In Bava Metzia 65a he said to Rav Pappa, ‘What did the master see?’ Bava Metzia 91b has Rav Shisha bar Rav Idi. Heilprin reports Sheshet in Rashi there [the checked Rashi reads Shisha]. Rav Shisha bar Rav Idi is one of two possible transmitters for Shmuel’s statement in Mo'ed Katan 14b. The other is Amemar. Rav Shisha bar Rav Idi transmitted a teaching of Rav Shmuel bar Yitzhak: Rosh Hashanah 27a. Yoma 42a: Rav Shisha. Rav Sheshet bar Rav Idi bar Avin: Hullin 14b, 122b; Pesahim 84b; Keritot 23, end of a; Bava Metzia 6a. Rav Idi bar Shisha may be his son.
